page.overview:
What is Cars 3?

Cars 3 is Pixar's eighteenth feature film, and the second sequel to the 2006 and 2011 films Cars and Cars 2, released on June 16, 2017. It was directed by Brian Fee.

In May 2016, Fee gave the first details regarding the plot: the film sees Lightning McQueen, now a veteran in the racing world, facing the rise of a new generation of race cars epitomized by Jackson Storm. Following a defeat to Jackson Storm, Lightning enlists the help of a new trainee, Cruz Ramirez, a sleek female race car, to prepare him for the the Florida 500, in the hope that he can give a game-changing performance. Fee elaborated: "Think of where he'd be in his career now in real time. [Lightning] is not an old man, but he's one of the older cars on the circuit with new rookies coming in. People start to wonder and ask when he might retire."

Lightning McQueen, now a seven-time Piston Cup champion, is preparing for a race, when suddenly Mater visits him in his trailer to keep him company. Lightning, who appreciates his best friend not wanting him to be lonely, politely asks Mater to give him some quiet. Mater leaves and, after having a flashback of Doc Hudson in Willy's Butte in order to give him some motivation, Lightning soon leaves his trailer and is out on the track racing against various other racers, including his best friends Bobby Swift and Cal Weathers. They love teasing each other. The trio are fun to watch both on and off the track. If any member of the trio wins a race, they'll surely get pranked by the other two, with Lightning getting covered in foam and confetti in one race, and Cal getting his tires inflated and attached to Lightning McQueen balloons in another.

One day, during a race at the Copper Canyon Speedway, a rookie racer named Jackson Storm, who is part of the next generation of high-tech racers, comes out of nowhere and overtakes Lightning, Bobby and Cal on the final lap, winning the race. After the race, Lightning congratulates Storm for winning, but the latter makes thinly-veiled insults at the veteran. The following eight races all end with Storm winning and, while he does it, more next-generation racers appear on the track, replacing the so-called "veterans of yesterday", including Bobby and Cal, who end up either getting fired by their sponsors or simply deciding to retire in order to make way for the inevitable takeover of the Next-Gens in the Piston Cup. During the Los Angeles 500, the final race of the season, Lightning is one of the only veterans to have not yet been replaced and, with only 40 laps to go and after a rushed pit stop, Lightning finally takes the lead, but Storm quickly catches up to him and tells him to enjoy his retirement before overtaking him, with Danny Swervez and Chase Racelott doing the same, as Lightning drops back to 4th place. Lightning tries his hardest to catch up to the three, but loses control, hits the wall and ends up experiencing a rollover crash.
